chunk_map.heading: ## How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 10 chunks. Chunk 8 line 66 `grep -n "Optional. They sit" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` -> `66:Optional. They sit in the gap before it. Do them and its moves land as things you've already seen.` — "They/them" resolve to the plural noun "Pre-reads" in the chunk's own header (line 64, in-chunk per rule), "it/its" resolve to "Module 2" named in the same header. Losing the numeral "All four" (per queue note) removed a quantity, not the antecedent — resolution intact. Generic nouns "the agent"/"the fix" (chunks 5, 7) read as established course vocabulary for AE101's single running bug-fix thread, not ambiguous pronouns. Harm check: rule exists to stop a slide the reader can't follow because a term points nowhere; no such gap found, so no REVISE.

Chunk 8 line 70 `grep -n "which is where Module 2 goes next"` -> `70:...The cure he lands on is human review made affordable by upfront planning, which is where Module 2 goes next.` and chunk 9 line 76 name Module 2 directly by title, not by page position relative to another file. No 'the opening lecture said' style unlocated callback found anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n "you just met" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` -> `52:[The machine you just met](lectures/the-machine-you-just-met.md)`. This link sits in chunk 6's Start Here menu, after the four in-class exercises in the same list (lines 44-50), so by the time a student reaches it in delivery order the referenced beat has occurred — file exists and is part of this module's own exercise/lecture set. No dead-beat reference found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a module overview/menu file (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, room norms, Start Here links, Key Concepts, Pre-reads, Next) — it carries no guess-before-reveal live-demo instruction itself; those beats live in the linked exercises/lectures.

All 10 chunks carry a self-standing claim (title/pacing note, Big Idea claim, Prework instructions, LO bullets, room-norm bullets, autonomy bullets, Start-here question+menu, Key Concepts recap, annotated reading list, closing bridge). None is a bare wait-state.

Checked each header against its own chunk content (e.g. `## Key Concepts` at line 56 followed only by concept-recap bullets 57-62; `## Next` at line 76 followed only by the Module-2 bridge at line 77). No header contradicted by its own chunk.

`grep -n "Not too fast, not too slow" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` -> `30:- Set the right pace for the group. Not too fast, not too slow.` is a single two-part idiom in one sentence, not the banned three-sentence "Not X. Not Y. Z." tic. `grep -n "his single biggest"` -> `74:...Cherny calls parallel worktrees his single biggest productivity unlock...` is reported attribution to Cherny, not the file's own self-grading superlative (the value-prop-leak sub-item targets the file praising itself/its own exercise, not quoting an external practitioner's opinion). No anaphora triples, number+retraction, abstraction-noun stacks, or empty-leg verb triplets found in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE "\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections)\b" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` returns hits only at lines 81+ (all inside the `<!-- maintainer -->` block starting line 79, out of body scope). Body (lines 1-78) contains none of these terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 `## What You'll Learn` (lines 14-21) bolds one lead verb per bullet (Run/Distinguish/Fix/Close/Compound) = 5 bolded elements on one slide; chunk 4 `## How we work in this room` (lines 22-27) bolds `**All learners.**`, `**Exercises.**`, `**Share and discuss.**` = 3 bolded elements on one slide. Both exceed the ≤1-bolded-element-per-slide budget and are not covered by the 2026-08-13 reading-list/lookup-surface carve-out (these are LO bullets and room-norm bullets, not a scanned menu). Harm check: the rule exists so one bolded handle carries visual priority on a projected slide; here every bullet leads bold, so nothing is differentiated — the harm the rule guards against (a wall of bold that reads as noise, not a handle) is technically present. However per the run queue's explicit note this is a known, already-logged standing TODO with the maintainer covering "bolded lead words on every What-You'll-Learn and room-agreement bullet" as a corpus-wide house convention, not a defect unique to this file — filed as non-blocking TODO, consistent with the prior verdict, not re-argued as new.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Leave as-is per standing maintainer TODO; if/when the corpus-wide convention is revisited, flatten LO/room-norm bullets to plain or single-handle bold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a module file rendered wholesale under a top-level `section.module` wrapper (per rule 10's own text, module files reach the composed deck via that wrapper, distinct from the phase-less prework/reference/supplementary pages that were previously dropped). No phase-less orphan section exists in this file's body.
